hesitations.reason: The rule was clear but gives an odd result. Step 1 reads his build tooltip, which says he flies a combat drone at aircraft and vehicles, and that names no role label. At step 4 his main weapon, the pistol, has no bonus, and official strength wording tied to another weapon (the drone) does not count there. The makers' 'early game anti-tank infantry' label counts only for roles.secondary. So step 5 gives the generalist role: he is slow, so assault. A fit_note says anti-armour is wanted.

alternatives: anti-air at step 1 instead of step 3
hesitations.reason: Anti-armour comes in at step 1 through the 20 May 2025 'anti-tank infantry' wording. Anti-air comes in at step 3. The open point is whether a tooltip that names the drone's targets ('against air units and vehicles') is a label under can_target step 3. I read it as a label for the weapon, not as words about the unit's own job. Scout fails its requires. The only part that might meet them is the Ambush Protocols doctrine's cloak, which the registry keeps off, and scout would rank third anyway.

The registry says to record a spawned helper with its owner. The drone flies and fights by itself, which matches the drone-launcher family's meaning. No rule says whether the family should come from the helper's own gun instead.

unclear_rules.topic: A soldier who parks to fly a drone
unclear_rules.note: The table in research/registry-notes/patterns.md folds this into launch-drones (piloted variant) with crew model remote. The correction at the top of the same file says a remote-piloted drone is the crew model remote, not launch-drones. launch-drones' summary is about releasing drones on a key. The remote crew model's coding-rule example matches the Drone Operator exactly, yet its rules exclude infantry and organic units. One explicit rule for an owner unit with a drone it can take over is needed.

The range bands do not say whether a drone weapon's reach is the drone's own gun range (here short) or how far from its owner the drone fights (medium by his attack reach, long with the Remote Control leash; the family default is long).

unclear_rules.topic: Doctrines that change a shared status
unclear_rules.note: EM Interference makes every Marked enemy silenced. The Doctrine page lists the markers (the Sentinel among them), while the Status effect page ties the silence to the status itself. It is unclear whether this is a new effect for named units (record it with source commander-power) or a side-wide change (leave it off). The registry line that 'the Ambush Protocols doctrine's wider stealth stays off' also leaves open whether 'wider' covers the drones' new stealth or only the longer stealth of units that already hide.

In Tempest Rising, silence blocks only active and passive abilities. Our silence weapon trait means the target can neither fire nor use abilities, so the game's narrower effect has no term or pattern.

unclear_rules.topic: The mark trait in Tempest Rising
unclear_rules.note: The trait says the team sees the target and hits it harder. The game's Marked status gives an Intel bounty and a bonus to Networked weapons, with no reveal. The registry tells coders to use the trait anyway.

unclear_rules.topic: A tooltip that names a weapon's targets
unclear_rules.note: The tooltip's line that he flies a combat drone at aircraft and vehicles could be a label under can_target step 3 and roles.secondary step 3, or strength wording for roles.primary step 4. The registry lists 'effective against' but not a bare 'against'. I treated it as a label for the drone only.

unclear_rules.topic: Deploy or toggle when only the controlled drone moves
unclear_rules.note: The ability-kinds tie-break speaks of 'the unit'. For an operator who stands rooted while his drone flies, I read 'the unit' as the operator.
The damage map leaves out the game's armour-ignoring type, and step 5 then forces the family default (kinetic for the Sentinel's scanner rounds).

unclear_rules.topic: Body plan for a scout car
unclear_rules.note: Open-mount needs exposed crew, hull-turret is for tanks and box-carrier needs passenger room. No plan covers an armoured or scout car with one small gun when the sources do not describe the mount.

new_mechanics.summary: An effect stops enemies from using their active and passive abilities while it lasts, but leaves them free to move and attack; here the EM Interference doctrine applies it to every enemy the GDF has Marked. Counterplay: stay unmarked by keeping away from the marking units or killing them, or wait out the mark before relying on abilities.

source_problems:
Copy-check: every page came from the cache; nothing failed to fetch. The pages themselves have these problems:
(1) The Drone Operator page lags patch 2.0.0. Its infobox speed is the 1.9.0 value, and the 2.0.0 notes raise it a little.
(2) The Combat Drone page is verified only at 1.6.0+53654. Its multiplayer health predates Hotfix Update #8, which raised it, as the page's own changelog also says. It also calls combat drones 'uncontrollable', which clashes with the Drone Operator's Remote Control button, his Codex text, his build tooltip and StrategyWiki.
(3) The GDF Barracks page, which holds the Drone Operator's build tooltip, is verified only at 1.4.0.
(4) The GDF Arsenal line for the Drone Operator (a soldier against vehicles and aircraft who also spots) is carried by no official Steam post found back to 2022, so it does not count.
(5) StrategyWiki's 'Tempest Rising/GDF units' page shows pre-release values: Drone Operator price 220 against 370, Sentinel health 250 against 260.
(6) The Drone Operator page says the drone outranges basic anti-ground base defences, yet the Gatling Turret reaches about twice the micromissiles' range. The claim probably means flying the drone in by hand, or defences that cannot fire at aircraft.
(7) The Sentinel page is verified only at 1.6.0+53654. The wiki's patch pages from 1.6.0+53840 to 2.0.1+60808 change nothing on it. Its weapon box says the scanner rounds are 'rapidly fired', while the infobox has them firing half as often as the minigun. Its doctrine list includes Efficient Intel, which has no visible effect on it.
(8) No source says how the Sentinel's gun is mounted. The only hint about its look is design trivia (a futuristic Hummer concept).
